key_idea: Turn global density into a local score on hybrid Delaunay/Voronoi decomposition stars, then rule out every possible counterexample by enumerating tame graphs and bounding each one with linear programs and interval-arithmetic inequalities.
reason: The localization through a hybrid score function is a real and clever idea. Almost all the work, though, is done by machine enumeration of thousands of tame graphs, about 10^5 linear programs and more than 23,000 interval-arithmetic cases, so a reader cannot see why fcc is optimal beyond the fact that every case was checked.
recognized: Hales (with Ferguson), proof of the Kepler conjecture, Annals of Mathematics 2005 / Discrete & Computational Geometry 2006
